You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like late 2016 or early 2017, most likely November or December 2016.

- The unemployment rate is 5.0% and the fed funds rate is 0.35%. That matches roughly late 2015 to November 2016, before the December 2016 hike took the rate to 0.54%.
- Core CPI is 2.02% and headline CPI is 0.44%. That fits late 2015 to mid 2016.
- The 10-year yield is 2.31% and the 2-year is 1.08%. That rules out mid 2016, when the 10-year was about 1.5%, and a 10-year of 2.31% fits December 2015 (2.24%).
- The fed funds rate rose after the December 2015 hike, so a rate of 0.35% points to December 2015 or January 2016. The 12-month change of +0.29 fits December 2015, when the rate was about 0.24% at the end of the month.
- The 3-month change in the 2-year yield is +0.44 and the 2-year is 1.08%. The 2-year was about 1.06% in December 2015, which fits.
- Industrial production is -1.17% YoY, and the dollar is up 10.5% YoY. Both fit late 2015.
- VIX is 17.29, down 7.2 over three months. That fits December 2015 after the August 2015 spike.
- Emerging-market equity is down 16% over 12 months and gold is down 10.7%, which also fits 2015.
- US large-cap equity is -2.7% over one month, which fits December 2015.
- The unemployment rate is 5.0%, which matches December 2015.

I settle on December 2015.
